items.title: Emile Barnes and Paul Barnes Interview, 1959-10-01
items.q: Some of this book I believe did you once loan this to Walter Allen? Yeah, I did.

ctx.x: Real well then. And then later I'll come to the part where he began to fail. So after leaving Quag, after that job was up, then it was up to 1930. You see I played around with different bands up until 1931. I was playing with Richard Cheaterman in what you call a taxi dancing school they called up there. Then King Oliver came back with the band and asked me to make a trip with him. That was in 1931. Well John Marrero was to go on the trip but he was in bed with the union. He didn't make the trip. So in 1931 we…

Some of this book I believe did you once loan this to Walter Allen? Yeah, I did. And I think he published that in an article, some of it in the record changer. I guess you got that paper that time. Wow. Called the King's Saxophone, remember that article.
I didn't get it. You didn't see it. I have it. You don't have it now.
